edinburgh_home_b_ferguson.text: Gardyloo! That was the old cry from an upstairs window before someone emptied a bucket in the street. It comes from the French for watch out for the water.
The Old Town built up and up because it was squeezed inside the city wall. Some of the tenements climbed ten or eleven storeys, long before anyone said skyscraper.

then.text: Back for the Haggis, Neeps and Tatties? Kitchen's yours.

else.text: Is it Burns Night? It's always Burns Night in this house.
Neeps are swede, not turnip, whatever the shop says. Mash them with plenty of butter and pepper. Then a wee dram of gravy over the lot.
Pop in whenever you've got the makings. Use my kitchen.
